prompt: Write exactly one literal, factual sentence (8–14 words) describing only visible content in the image. Preferred concise template: Primary subject + one or two high‑signal attribute(s) + action/pose + location/nearby object. High‑signal attributes = specific object type (e.g., fountain, electric guitar), visible color/pattern, clear count (two, three), clothing/accessory, or legible text/logo. Require at least one high‑signal token and permit a second when clearly visible. Place at least one high‑signal token within the first three words (e.g., subject immediately followed by attribute: “woman red bicycle …”). Keep attribute and noun adjacent (prefer “red bicycle” not “bicycle that is red”) and favor compact, noun‑rich phrasing; avoid filler words and adverbs. If text/logo is legible, include the exact text verbatim as a high‑signal token and place it early when natural. Use exact numerals when each item is fully visible; if >3 or indistinct use “several”; if uncertain, omit counts. Do not infer unseen attributes (age, emotion, relationships, intent) and do not use figurative, evaluative, or subjective language. Use “person” if gender or age is unclear; use “man,” “woman,” or “child” only when clearly visible. Output exactly one short sentence only — no labels, examples, lists, or extra text.
